mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: No statistically significant negative correlation (p > 0.05) between GDPC1 YoY < -2% and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (p > 0.10) when UNRATE > 4.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship (p > 0.05) between four-month INDPRO decline and S&P 500 60-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 3% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing, which lowers risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 3% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% over three months signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by >1% over three months
failure_condition: No significant negative correlation (p > 0.10) between joint UNRATE rise and PAYEMS fall and S&P 500 20-day returns.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that above-trend RSAFS growth predicts positive equity returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation (p > 0.05) between above-trend RSAFS growth and S&P 500 5-day returns in out-of-sample test.
